jobs.title: KASA saglik kapisi: browser ac + fingerprint olcumu (adversary_site.py)
jobs.fix_spec: Create the COMPLETE file _orch/loop/browser_gate.py for Project KASA's autonomous fix-loop. It launches the REAL KASA browser after a code fix and checks it is not broken and does not leak fingerprint data, using the existing measurement harness _orch/redteam/adversary_site.py. Implement EXACTLY: Constants REPO=r'd:/kasa'; ADV_DIR=REPO+'/_orch/redteam'; CAPTURES=ADV_DIR+'/captures.jsonl'; ADV_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8901/?pass=1'; PY=sys.executable. start_adversary(): add ADV_DIR to sys.path, import the adversary_site module, run its ThreadedHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1:8901 inside a daemon thread; return an object with a .stop() method that shuts the server down cleanly so the port is free for the next call. launch_kasa(timeout_s): truncate CAPTURES to empty (create parent dir if needed); env = os.environ.copy() with KASA_HEALTHCHECK_URL=ADV_URL and KASA_HEALTHCHECK_MS=str(max(1,timeout_s-2)*1000); subprocess.Popen([PY,'-c',"import sys;sys.path.insert(0,r'd:/kasa');from src.browser.browser_window import open_browser;open_browser()"], cwd=REPO, env=env); wait up to timeout_s seconds, kill if still alive. read_captures(): parse CAPTURES as one JSON object per line, return [] if missing/empty. evaluate(records) -> (ok, report): boot_ok=len(records)>=1; pick the last record with pass==2, else the last record, else None; leaks=[] from that record's js/http: 'webgl' if a real GPU marker (RTX/GeForce/Radeon <model>/'NVIDIA ') appears in js.get('webglRenderer',''); 'accept_language' if http.get('accept_language','').split(',')[0].strip().lower() != js.get('language','').lower(); 'timezone' if js.get('timezone')!='Europe/Berlin' or js.get('tzOffset') is not consistent with Europe/Berlin's CURRENT DST offset (hint: use zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('Europe/Berlin') + datetime.now() to compute the expected getTimezoneOffset()-style value); 'platform' if js.get('platform')!='Win32'. report={'boot_ok':boot_ok,'leaks':leaks,'sample':record}. run_gate(mode='boot', timeout_s=16) -> (ok, report): start_adversary(); try launch_kasa(timeout_s); records=read_captures(); ok,report=evaluate(records); finally always call adversary.stop(). mode=='boot' => ok=report['boot_ok']; mode=='fingerprint' => ok=report['boot_ok'] and not report['leaks']. NEVER let an exception escape run_gate: catch everything, return (False,{'error': str(e)}). Add if __name__=='__main__': print(json.dumps(run_gate('fingerprint'), default=str, indent=2)). Output ONLY the complete file in one ```python``` block.
jobs.checklist: 1. run_gate/launch_kasa/start_adversary/read_captures/evaluate all present. 2. mode=boot -> ok=boot_ok; mode=fingerprint -> ok=boot_ok and not leaks. 3. No path raises; all exceptions caught -> (False,{'error':...}). 4. KASA_HEALTHCHECK_URL/MS set in subprocess env, cwd=REPO. 5. adversary .stop() always called (finally). Valid Python 3.

jobs.title: WebGL2 baglaminda GPU spoof yok (WebGL1-only patch sizinti birakiyordu)
jobs.fix_spec: Project KASA's browser_window.py has a WebGL fingerprint-poisoning block (search for the comment 'WebGL Fingerprint Poisoning') that already patches WebGLRenderingContext.prototype.getParameter using a seeded random index stored in sessionStorage as '_kp_webgl_idx' (only active when POISON is true, i.e. LEVEL is 'strict' or 'paranoid'). The bug: modern pages/tests often use a WebGL2 context, and WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.getParameter is a SEPARATE, unpatched function, so the real GPU renderer/vendor leaks through WebGL2 even though WebGL1 is spoofed. Below is the CURRENT full file. Return the COMPLETE fixed file. Preserve ALL existing behavior EXACTLY EXCEPT: inside the same WebGL Fingerprint Poisoning block, ALSO patch WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.getParameter with the SAME logic and the SAME '_kp_webgl_idx' seed value as the WebGL1 patch (do not introduce a new/different seed or a different fake value set -- WebGL1 and WebGL2 must return IDENTICAL spoofed values on the same page, otherwise the mismatch itself becomes a new fingerprinting signal). Guard the WebGL2 patch with 'if (typeof WebGL2RenderingContext !== "undefined")' so it doesn't throw on contexts without WebGL2 support. Do not touch canvas poisoning, tracker cookie poisoning, WebRTC layer, or anything outside this block. Output ONLY the complete fixed file in one python block.
jobs.checklist: 1. WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.getParameter is patched inside the WebGL Fingerprint Poisoning block. 2. It reuses '_kp_webgl_idx' (same variable, same fake-value logic) as the WebGL1 patch -- values must match between WebGL1 and WebGL2. 3. Guarded with a typeof check so it's safe if WebGL2 is unsupported. 4. WebGL1 patch (webglProto.getParameter) untouched. 5. Nothing outside the WebGL block changed. Valid Python 3.

jobs.title: Paranoid seviyede bilinen tracker istekleri engellenmiyor (etikette vaat var, kod yok)
jobs.fix_spec: Project KASA's browser_window.py privacy-level UI already labels 'paranoid' as 'Siki + bilinen tracker istekleri engellenir (deneysel)' but NO code actually blocks tracker requests at any level -- this is a missing feature, not a bug fix. Below is the CURRENT full file. Return the COMPLETE fixed file. Preserve ALL existing behavior EXACTLY, and ADD a new block (place it right after the existing 'Known Tracker Cookie Poisoning' block) that: (1) defines a small JS array constant named EXACTLY 'KASA_TRACKER_DOMAINS' containing 8-15 well-known third-party tracker/analytics hostnames as substrings (e.g. 'doubleclick.net', 'google-analytics.com', 'googletagmanager.com', 'facebook.net', 'connect.facebook.net', 'scorecardresearch.com', 'adnxs.com', 'criteo.com', 'hotjar.com', 'segment.io'); (2) ONLY when LEVEL === 'paranoid' (check the existing LEVEL variable from the level prelude -- do NOT change behavior for 'off'/'standard'/'strict'), wraps window.fetch so any request whose URL hostname contains one of KASA_TRACKER_DOMAINS resolves to a rejected/blocked Promise instead of firing; (3) ALSO patches XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open so that if the target URL contains one of KASA_TRACKER_DOMAINS, the request is silently no-op'd (does not call the original open, so .send() has nothing to send) instead of firing. Do not touch canvas/webgl poisoning, tracker COOKIE poisoning, WebRTC layer, or the LEVEL/POISON variables themselves. Output ONLY the complete fixed file in one python block.
jobs.checklist: 1. JS array KASA_TRACKER_DOMAINS with 8-15 known tracker hostnames. 2. window.fetch patched to block matching hostnames. 3. XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open patched to block matching hostnames. 4. All of this gated strictly behind LEVEL === 'paranoid' -- must not affect 'off'/'standard'/'strict' behavior at all. 5. Nothing else in the file changed. Valid Python 3.
